To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Community detection in networks with adaptive sampling strategies is fundamentally different from the classical problem of community extraction in stochastic block models, and that the latter problem can be solved accurately when the budget of observations is sufficiently large, while the former problem can be solved only approximately."

(a) for the stochastic block models with non adaptive sampling, there exist simple algorithms that accurately recover the communities if and only if the number of samples per node pair grows at least as fast as the square root of the number of nodes; (b) for the stochastic model with adaptive sampling, there also exists simple algorithms that accurately recovers the communities if and if the number of observations per node pair grows linearly with the number of nodes.

(i) the stochastic block model is not a necessary condition to detect communities; (ii) adaptive sampling is a key ingredient to detect communities; and (iii) the proposed adaptive sampling algorithms are optimal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a general problem of sampling a large data set, and then using the collected data to extract hidden information.
the design of sampling strategies and algorithms for community detection in large networks, and provides fundamental results for this problem.
the design of sampling and clustering strategies that jointly extract communities from a large data set.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a general framework for the problem of community detection via sampling, and we show how to design sampling and clustering strategies to accurately recover the hidden communities when this is possible.
we provide a unified framework for both random and adaptive sampling, and derive fundamental performance limits for community detection.

, in the context of community detection, random sampling is more powerful than adaptive sampling, in the sense that random sampling can achieve the optimal performance, while adaptive sampling can only achieve sub-optimal performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of the recovered communities is not only determined by the budget of samples, but also by the sampling strategy used.
the accuracy of community detection can be significantly improved by designing a sequence of node pairs to be sampled in an adaptive way, based on previous observations.
adaptive sampling strategies can lead to significant performance gains over non adaptive strategies, in terms of the number of required samples to achieve accurate community detection.
